figures.detail: Hetzner CAX21, lagom-shared-02, in fsn1. It has hosted prod and staging since 2026-10-28. The previous node, a CAX11 in nbg1, was deleted on 2026-11-07.

figures.detail: On lagom-shared-02. The rest of the nominal 8 GB is reserved by firmware and the kernel.

figures.label: Outside Kubernetes
figures.detail: RSS on 2026-10-28, two hours after k3s started, with 12 Pods running: k3s-server 1,022, containerd 200, 12 shims 254, tailscaled 55, the rest of the OS ~156.

figures.label: Request ceiling, enforced in CI
figures.detail: 5,632 MiB. It sits ~420 MiB under what remains after the overhead above: 7,741 MiB visible minus 1,687 MiB. A change that would exceed the ceiling fails the build. On the 4 GB node the ceiling was 2.2 GB.

figures.label: Declared requests today
figures.detail: Dagster in both environments, each 800 resident and 768 per run, and cloudflared at 48. It was 5,582, 50 MiB under the ceiling, until the two CronJobs on Postgres were retired on 2026-11-07, which freed 256 each.

figures.label: RAM this site uses on the node
figures.detail: The architecture table lists the site at 0. The pages are static files. Nothing on the node serves them.

figures.label: Rebuild, measured
figures.detail: From the first command on the node to prod's first green run, on 2026-10-28, moving from lagom-shared-01 to lagom-shared-02. Provisioning was not included. About 6 minutes of it was the machine working; the rest was the operator reading results and starting the next step. A rebuild from nothing is described as about 50 minutes, and that figure is an estimate, not a measurement.

figures.label: The feed
figures.detail: Refreshed every few minutes, no API key, no practical rate limit. Ready-made windows cover the past hour, the past day and the past 30 days. Each event carries magnitude, depth, coordinates, a timestamp and a place.

figures.value: Catalog in Postgres, files on R2
figures.label: Where the lake target points
figures.detail: The proposed SME stack: DuckDB is the engine, DuckLake the table format, Postgres the catalog, the data files on Cloudflare R2. The orchestration section says the usgs job loads into that lake and dbt builds on the lake target. The storage section says this replaces Postgres only after the spike passes.

figures.label: The usgs job
figures.detail: At :00 and :30 UTC. dlt loads the events updated since the last cursor into DuckLake (bronze.usgs_events), then dbt build runs on the lake target and runs their 33 tests.

figures.label: Bronze freshness, as recorded
figures.detail: Checked by dbt source freshness, which dbt build does not run. The roadmap item that declares and asserts a freshness threshold is still open.

figures.label: Prod's first lake run
figures.detail: 2026-11-05 12:00 UTC. Loaded 30 days. dbt reported PASS=33.

figures.label: Memory of that first prod run
figures.detail: Steps in one process. The next run was 442 MiB. Samples are 2–15 s apart and miss short peaks, so the true peak may be higher.

figures.label: Request for each run
figures.detail: The limit is 1 GiB. The request stays at 768: the samples are 2–15 s apart and miss short peaks, and lowering it by 64–128 MiB would need a new image.

figures.label: Staging, first week
figures.detail: usgs runs succeeded, 2026-10-28 to 11-05. Median 43 s, maximum 136 s. The one failure was a driver pitfall recorded in the runbook.
figures.source: docs/architecture.md, Dagster (M3); the count is also in docs/roadmap.md, M3

figures.label: One timed run
figures.detail: The 21:30 run of 2026-10-28. The rest was Dagster's own start-up and per-step overhead.

figures.label: An incremental run
figures.detail: Started on demand at 11:17 UTC on 2026-11-05. PASS=33, in under a minute.

figures.label: Earlier peaks, two processes
figures.detail: During dbt build, when each step still ran in a second Python process. 6–8 samples each, so the true peak may be higher.

figures.label: Daily maintenance, first week
figures.detail: All 8 lake_maintenance runs succeeded. The job runs daily at 04:15 UTC: it merges small Parquet files, expires snapshots older than 7 days, and deletes files nothing references.

figures.label: CI, not a production load
figures.detail: dbt build on the lake target over a 12-row hand-made bronze fixture in a DuckLake on the runner, on 2026-11-07.

figures.label: The warehouse decision
figures.detail: The storage section says every layer lives in Postgres until the SME-stack spike passes. The orchestration section says the usgs job loads DuckLake and dbt builds on the lake target. The roadmap records both: the job runs on DuckLake, and the spike is still open. This page does not close that decision.
figures.source: docs/architecture.md §2 and §7; docs/roadmap.md, the trigger table and M3

figures.label: Files and bytes on R2
figures.detail: How many files the lake holds, and how many bytes, are not written in the architecture or the roadmap. This page does not estimate them.

figures.label: Dashboards
figures.detail: Evidence, the dashboard gallery, is a separate piece of the same milestone. It is not built in these pages.
